story.title: New Mexico Files Lawsuit Against DOJ and Todd Blanche Over Epstein Investigation Access
story.summary: The state of New Mexico has filed a lawsuit against the Department of Justice and Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche, claiming they obstructed the state's investigation into Jeffrey Epstein's alleged crimes. The lawsuit was filed on the same day that New Mexico released a report detailing preliminary findings from its ongoing probe into Epstein's activities at a ranch in Stanley.

event_overview.title: About Epstein Investigation
event_overview.subject: Epstein Investigation
event_overview.summary: The Epstein investigation refers to the overlapping U.S. criminal investigations, prosecutions, custody review, and later records-disclosure efforts concerning Jeffrey Epstein’s sexual exploitation and trafficking of minors, as well as alleged assistance by associates. It includes the 2019 federal case in New York, which ended after Epstein’s death, related proceedings involving Ghislaine Maxwell, and continuing disputes over access to Justice Department records.

facts.label: Federal criminal case
facts.value: A federal grand jury in the Southern District of New York returned an indictment in July 2019 charging Epstein with sex trafficking of minors and conspiracy to commit sex trafficking of minors; the alleged conduct covered 2002 through 2005 and included New York and Florida.

facts.label: Case outcome and continuing investigativ
facts.value: Epstein died in federal custody on August 10, 2019. The Southern District of New York formally dismissed the federal case on August 29, 2019, while stating that its investigation into his conduct continued.

facts.label: Custody review
facts.value: The Justice Department inspector general’s 2023 review focused on Bureau of Prisons personnel and identified serious failures at the Metropolitan Correctional Center in New York; it reported that Epstein died by suicide while in BOP custody.

facts.label: Related prosecution
facts.value: Ghislaine Maxwell, described by the Southern District of New York as Epstein’s longtime partner and co-conspirator, was convicted by a unanimous federal jury on December 29, 2021 for facilitating and participating in the sexual abuse of children.

facts.label: Records-disclosure framework
facts.value: The Epstein Files Transparency Act became Public Law 119-38 on November 19, 2025. It directs the Attorney General to publish unclassified DOJ records relating to Epstein, Maxwell, associated investigations, custodial matters, and specified related records, subject to protections including for victim-identifying information and child sexual-abuse material.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows notable later developments tied to people associated with Epstein and to access to federal investigative records; it does not attempt to catalog every allegation, civil case, prosecution, document release, or individual mentioned in the files.

related_stories.title: Israeli Settler Charged in Killing of Palestinian Activist Awdah Hathaleen
related_stories.summary: Israeli prosecutors have charged settler Yinon Levi with the killing of Palestinian activist Awdah Hathaleen in the occupied West Bank. The indictment, filed in district court, marks the first time an Israeli has been charged for the death of a Palestinian since the October 2023 attacks.

related_stories.title: Mexican Influencer César Gastélum Killed During Live Stream
related_stories.summary: César Gastélum, a popular Mexican social media influencer, was shot and killed while live streaming outside a fast-food restaurant in Culiacán, Sinaloa. The incident occurred on Tuesday evening, and Gastélum had nearly 600,000 followers on TikTok, where he was known for his comedy videos. He was reportedly attacked by a motorbike driver while filming with two friends.

related_stories.title: Ugandan Football Star David Owori Killed in Suspected Robbery Attack
related_stories.summary: David Owori, the captain of SC Villa and a Ugandan international football player, was found unconscious and later pronounced dead after being attacked by suspected robbers in Kampala. The 27-year-old reportedly resisted an attempted robbery, leading to his fatal injuries. His death has sparked outrage and raised concerns about rising violent crime in Uganda.

related_stories.title: Tarun Tejpal Receives 10-Year Sentence for Rape Conviction
related_stories.summary: Indian journalist Tarun Tejpal has been sentenced to 10 years in prison for rape. Tejpal, who has denied the allegations, plans to appeal the verdict in India's Supreme Court.
